key_insight: Physics-informed circuits, compact gauge-field digitization, and operator truncation advance hardware demonstrations toward real-time simulations of strongly interacting quantum fields.
engineering_relevance: These techniques reduce qubit and circuit-depth requirements for lattice-field simulations relevant to QCD dynamics.
method: Prepare interacting ground states and simulate a heavy quark traversing light quarks in 1+1D SU(2) lattice gauge theory.
Digitize a fully gauge-fixed SU(2) Hamiltonian in a mixed basis using as few as three qubits per plaquette.
Apply Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) during adiabatic preparation of a λφ⁴ ground state.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardware validation against classical benchmarks, low-energy observables reproduced to 10⁻³ precision with compact digitization, and about 30% circuit-depth reduction from SeqHT.
watch_item: Resource overhead still limits larger systems, and truncations must preserve the observables of interest.
paper_title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
